facts.text: The user wants to teach middle school students (ages 12–16) the basics of healthy and safe cooking.
The user wants to support learners to recall and process accurate foundational information without using quizzes.
The user believes quizzes enable short-term recall rather than long-term memorisation.
The user wants to use two instructional strategies proven to increase effective memorisation of foundational knowledge.
The user’s first instructional strategy is called Undoing.
The user wants Undoing activities used at the start of the learning process to identify and correct gaps in knowledge, misconceptions, and misplaced reasoning.
The user wants Undoing activities to ask learners to predict the outcome of a scenario.
The user provided an example undoing activity about a candle burning and Sharna’s ideas about what happened to the wax.
The user wants feedback written for each potential response that explains the difference between the student’s response and the correct answer.
The user wants the feedback to replace misconceptions with alternative conceptions and explain the correct way of thinking.
The user wants to suggest a resource for the defined learner type to learn the correct version of foundational cooking knowledge.
The user asked for one more activity similar to the previous one.
The user asked that the resource include a link or proper citation information.

events.text: Request to generate an undoing activity for middle school learners about core foundational knowledge for healthy meals
Request to generate one more similar undoing activity and provide a link or proper citation for the resource
